promptDecks.title: Toy Stories
promptDecks.description: A deck of playful prompts for using toys and figures to create stories, explore situations, and imagine what happens next.

promptDecks.title: Put It in Perspective
promptDecks.description: Helps clients step back from difficult situations, evaluate their size and lasting impact more realistically, and consider the bigger picture so one moment, mistake, feeling, or problem does not take over the whole story.

prompts.text: Think of something bothering you right now. How big does it feel in this moment?
Think of something bothering you right now. How important is it likely to feel a week from now?
Think of something bothering you right now. How important is it likely to feel a month from now?
Think of something bothering you right now. How important is it likely to feel a year from now?
Think of a recent problem that felt huge while it was happening. How does it feel looking back now?
Think of something you worried about last week. How much space does it take up in your mind today?
Think of something that once felt like a huge deal but barely matters to you now. What changed?
Think of a difficult moment that passed. What did you learn about how feelings can change with time?
Think of a problem that feels like it's taking over everything. What parts of your life are not this problem?
Think of a bad day you've had recently. What happened that made it bad, and what happened that wasn't bad?
Think of something going wrong in one area of your life. What other areas are still okay or going well?
Think of one relationship that's difficult right now. What other relationships exist in your life?
Think of one thing you're struggling with. What are some things you can still do well?
Think of one thing you don't like about yourself. What gets left out if you judge your whole self by that one thing?
Think of one mistake you've made. How much should one mistake get to say about who you are?
Think of one decision you regret. Does that decision represent every decision you've made?
Think of something you failed at. What does that outcome tell you, and what does it not tell you?
Think of something you haven't accomplished yet. What progress or effort might disappear if you focus only on the unfinished goal?
Think of a setback you've had. Is it the end of the story or one part of it?
Think of something that feels like starting over. What knowledge, experience, or strength are you bringing with you this time?
Think of something that didn't go according to plan. What is still possible from here?
Think of a situation where one thing went wrong. What else went right, okay, or simply didn't go wrong?
Think of a situation your brain summarizes as “everything went wrong.” What happened when you look at the individual pieces?
Think of a day your brain labeled “terrible.” If you divided it into individual moments, were they all terrible?
Think of a person you're frustrated with. Does the thing they did represent everything about them?
Think of someone you're angry with. What else is true about your relationship besides the current conflict?
Think of a disagreement that feels very important right now. What is the disagreement actually about?
Think of a conflict that became bigger than the original issue. What got added along the way?
Think of something someone said that keeps replaying in your mind. How much importance does that person's opinion deserve?
Think of criticism you've received. Is it information about one behavior, one situation, or your entire character?
Think of a compliment you've received. Does your brain give positive information as much attention as criticism?
Think of an awkward moment you keep replaying. How much time do you think other people have actually spent thinking about it?
Think of something embarrassing that happened to someone else. How long did you think about their embarrassment afterward?
Think of a social mistake you've made. If someone else made the same mistake, how important would it seem to you?
Think of something you worry other people noticed about you. What else were they probably paying attention to?
Think of a situation where you felt judged. How important is one person's judgment in the larger picture of who you are?
Think of someone who doesn't like you or might not like you. Does being disliked by one person mean you're unlikeable?
Think of a relationship that changed or ended. What did that relationship mean to you, and what parts of your life exist beyond it?
Think of a rejection you've experienced. What opportunities, relationships, or possibilities remained afterward?
Think of something you weren't chosen for. What other chances to participate, succeed, connect, or try again still exist?
Think of something you missed out on. What did you lose, and what did you not lose?
Think of something you wish had happened differently. What can still happen next?
Think of something you cannot change. How much of your future does that one event get to determine?
Think of something painful from your past. What parts of you have developed since it happened?
Think of a difficult period in your life. What else was happening in your life at the same time?
Think of a difficult period that eventually changed. What would the version of you living through it have been surprised to know?
Think of a feeling that seems enormous right now. Is the size of the feeling the same as the size of the problem?
Think of a time you had a huge emotional reaction to a relatively small event. What else might have been contributing?
Think of a situation that seems small to other people but feels important to you. Why does it matter to you?
Can something be genuinely painful without being catastrophic? What would that distinction mean?
Can something matter without needing to take over everything else?
Can a problem be serious and still be manageable?
Can something be unfair and still be something you can cope with?
Can something be disappointing without meaning everything is ruined?
Can something be embarrassing without being permanently damaging?
Can someone be upset with you without the relationship being destroyed?
Can someone dislike a choice you made without disliking you as a person?
Can you perform poorly at something without being bad at it?
Can you struggle with something without being a failure?
Can you make a bad choice without being a bad person?
Can you regret something without needing to punish yourself forever?
Can you have a bad day without being back at the beginning?
Can symptoms return without erasing the progress you've made?
Can you need help and still be capable?
Can you feel overwhelmed and still take one useful step?
Can you feel hopeless without knowing that the future is hopeless?
Think of something your brain calls a disaster. What was actually lost, harmed, or changed?
Think of something your brain calls “the worst.” Compared with what?
Think of something your brain says you “ruined.” Which parts are actually ruined, and which parts can still be repaired?
Think of something your brain says “everyone” noticed. How many people actually noticed?
Think of something your brain says you'll “never get over.” What experiences from your past show that intensity can change?
Think of something your brain says “changes everything.” What things would actually remain unchanged?
Think of something your brain says you “can't come back from.” What would coming back from it realistically mean?
Think of something your brain keeps replaying. Is replaying it helping you solve something, or making the moment feel permanently present?
Think of a problem that takes up a lot of mental space. How much actual time does the problem occupy compared with how much time you spend thinking about it?
Think of something you're worried about tomorrow. How much of today do you want the worry to take?
Think of a future event you're anxious about. How long will the actual event last?
Think of something you're dreading. What happens before and after that moment?
Think of an upcoming challenge. Where does it fit within the rest of your week, month, or year?
Think of a goal that feels overwhelming. What is the next piece rather than the entire journey?
Think of something you need to accomplish. What would “good enough for now” look like?
Think of something you're putting enormous pressure on yourself to do well. How important is doing it perfectly compared with doing it at all?
Think of a decision that feels enormous. Is it permanent, reversible, adjustable, or something you can learn from?
Think of a choice you're afraid of getting wrong. What options would still exist afterward?
Think of a consequence you're worried about. How long would that consequence realistically last?
Think of a feared outcome. If it happened, what would likely happen the next day?
Think of a feared outcome. What would likely happen a week afterward?
Think of a feared outcome. What parts of your life would continue?
Think of something that feels impossible right now. What would make it 10% more manageable?
Think of something that feels like a 10 out of 10 problem. What makes it a 10?
Think of a problem that feels huge. If 10 meant immediate danger or permanent devastation, where would this problem actually belong?
Think of a problem that seems small but keeps affecting you. What makes it deserve attention even if it isn't a crisis?
Think of two problems you've faced recently. Which one needs your attention first, and why?
Think of something you're spending a lot of energy on. Does its importance match the amount of energy it's receiving?
Think of something you have very little control over. How much of your energy do you want it to receive?
Think of something you can influence. What part deserves your attention?
Think of a situation where you can't control the outcome. What can you still control about your response?
Imagine your current problem is one chapter in a long book about your life. What might the chapter be called?
Imagine zooming out from this week and looking at your whole year. How much space does this problem take up?
Imagine looking back at this situation five years from now. What do you think you'll remember most?
Imagine your future self looking back on what you're dealing with now. What might they understand that is difficult to see from inside the situation?
Imagine someone you care about was experiencing exactly what you're experiencing. How big would you tell them the problem is?
Imagine you could put the problem on a table and walk around it. What might you notice from another side?
Imagine your attention is a spotlight. What is it shining on right now, and what is sitting outside the light?
Imagine your brain has zoomed all the way in on one bad detail. What becomes visible when you zoom back out?
What is one fact about your situation that makes it difficult?
What is one fact about your situation that makes it manageable?
What is one thing the problem has changed?
What is one thing the problem has not changed?
What is one thing you've lost sight of because this problem has been taking up so much attention?
What is one strength you still have even while this problem is happening?
What is one source of support that still exists?
What is one choice you still have?
What is one thing you can do next?
What is one problem in your life right now that might look different if you zoomed out and saw the whole picture?

promptDecks.title: Role Play
promptDecks.description: A deck of prompts for acting out situations, practicing different responses, and exploring what could happen next.

Pretend you need a few minutes alone. Show me how you let someone know.
Pretend you changed your mind about something. Show me how you tell someone.
Pretend you are nervous about trying something new. Show me what happens.
Pretend you have to walk into a room where you do not know anyone. Show me what you do.

Pretend you are in charge of making one rule for all kids. Tell me the rule and show me why it matters.

Pretend you are teaching a class called “How to Understand Grown-Ups.” I am your student. Teach me something.
Pretend you are an expert on friendship and I have come to you with a friendship problem. Give me advice.
Pretend you are an expert on worries and I have a ridiculous worry. Show me what your expert says.
Pretend you are an expert on anger and I keep getting mad about tiny things. Show me what your expert teaches me.
Pretend you are an expert on mistakes and I think mistakes are terrible. Convince me otherwise.
Pretend you are an expert on having bad days. Teach me how to survive one.
Pretend you are my coach and I have to do something scary. Show me how you coach me.
Pretend you are my confidence coach and I think I cannot do something. Show me what you say.
Pretend you are my problem-solving coach and my first plan failed. Help me come up with another.
Pretend you are the world's worst advice giver. I have a problem. Give me hilariously terrible advice.
Pretend you are the world's best advice giver. I have a silly problem. Tell me what to do.

promptDecks.title: Anger, Frustration & Irritability
promptDecks.description: Helps clients understand anger, frustration, and irritability by exploring triggers, body signals, thoughts, urges, underlying emotions, and ways to express and respond to these feelings effectively.

Think of something that became automatic over time. What helped it become automatic?

Think of a setback where your brain says, “I ruined it.” What remains unruined?

Think of something where you keep changing strategies. How long would you need to try one approach before you could evaluate it fairly?
Think of a task you dread. What is the hardest moment: anticipating it, starting it, doing it, or finishing it?

Think of a task where finishing is the hardest part. What happens when you're almost done?
Think of a task where stopping is difficult. What could help you recognize when enough is enough?
Think of a task you tend to overdo once you start. How could you plan a stopping point?
Think of something where you burn yourself out trying to make progress quickly. What pace would be easier to maintain?
Think of something you approach with “all or nothing” effort. What would sustainable effort look like?
Think of a goal where rest is part of succeeding rather than a break from succeeding.
Think of a goal where pushing harder isn't helping. What might happen if you adjusted the plan instead?
Think of something you need support with. What kind of support would actually improve follow through?
Think of something where having another person nearby helps you start. How could you intentionally use that support?
Think of something where accountability helps you. Who could you tell about your plan?
Think of something where accountability makes you feel pressured or ashamed. What kind of support would work better?
Think of something you want someone to remind you about. Would the reminder help, or would it make you resist doing it?
Think of a goal where encouragement helps. What kind of encouragement works for you?
Think of a goal where praise doesn't help much. What does help you keep going?
Think of something where you need practical help rather than encouragement. What could you ask for?
Think of something where you need company rather than advice. How could you ask for that?
Think of something where you need fewer demands rather than more motivation. What could be removed or postponed?
Think of a time when you have too many goals at once. Which one deserves priority?
Think of several things you want to change. Which change would make the others easier?
Think of something important that keeps losing to urgent tasks. How could you protect time for it?
Think of something you keep saying is a priority. Does the way you spend your time reflect that?
Think of something you spend a lot of time on that isn't actually important to you. What keeps pulling you toward it?
Think of a goal competing with something else you value. How could both needs get some space?
Think of a goal that may need to wait because something more important needs your energy right now. What would intentionally postponing it look like?
Think of something you're trying to force yourself to do despite being overloaded. Would reducing another demand help more than pushing harder?
Think of a day where your plan became impossible because something unexpected happened. How could you adjust without abandoning the whole day?
Think of a plan that depends on everything going right. What is your backup version?
Think of something you want to do tomorrow. What is most likely to get in the way?
Think of something you want to do tomorrow. What could you decide today so you don't have to decide in the moment?
Think of something you want to do this week. When specifically could it fit?
Think of something you want to do this week. What needs to happen beforehand?
Think of something you want to do this week. What could make it easier to begin when the time comes?
Think of something you want to do this week. What will you do if the original plan doesn't work?
Think of a situation where you tend to say, “I'll see how I feel.” What usually happens when the time arrives?
Think of something important that you frequently skip when you don't feel like doing it. Would deciding in advance help?
Think of something where flexibility is more useful than a strict schedule. What would a flexible plan look like?
Think of something where a specific time would make follow through more likely. What time makes sense?
Think of something where location matters. Where would it be easiest to do?
Think of something where another activity could serve as a cue. What could you connect it to?
Think of something where having materials ready would help. What could you prepare?
Think of something where your phone distracts you. What could you change before starting?
Think of something where interruptions derail you. What could protect a short period of time?
Think of something where you underestimate how long it takes. What could you change about the plan?
Think of something where you overestimate how long it takes and avoid starting. How could you find out how long it actually takes?
Think of a task where you lose track of time. What external cue could help?
Think of something where stopping to choose each next step drains your energy. What could you decide ahead of time?
Think of a routine with too many decisions. What could become a default?
Think of a repeated task you could make easier with a checklist.
Think of a repeated problem you keep solving from scratch. What could you set up once and reuse?
Think of something where you're relying on memory when you could rely on a system. What system could help?
Think of something where you keep blaming yourself for not following through. Is there something about the system that needs to change?
Think of a goal you've called yourself lazy for not completing. What other explanations deserve consideration?
Think of something you've struggled to do because you're overwhelmed. What would reduce the overwhelm?
Think of something you've struggled to do because it's boring. What could make it more engaging or tolerable?
Think of something you've struggled to do because it feels meaningless. Could connecting it to a larger purpose help?
Think of something you've struggled to do because you're afraid of the outcome. What part is an action problem, and what part is an anxiety problem?
Think of something you've struggled to do because you don't know how. What information or skill do you need?
Think of something you've struggled to do because the instructions are unclear. What could make the task more concrete?
Think of something you've struggled to do because there are too many steps in your head at once. What could you put outside your head?
Think of something you've struggled to do because you lose momentum after interruptions. What could help you find your place again?
Think of something you've struggled to do because you forget why it matters. What could remind you?
Think of something you've struggled to do because the reward is too far away. What could make progress rewarding sooner?
Think of something you've struggled to do because you expect yourself to do it in a way that doesn't work for you. What could you customize?
Think of a goal you're currently pursuing. What is the action, rather than the outcome?
Think of a goal that depends on another person's response. How could you rewrite your part so success is within your control?
Think of a goal like “make friends.” What actions could you control even though you can't control whether a friendship develops?
Think of a goal like “stop being anxious.” What actions could you take even if anxiety remains?
Think of a goal like “be more confident.” What would you do differently if you were acting with more confidence?
Think of a goal like “be happier.” What experiences or behaviors could you increase?
Think of a goal like “stop procrastinating.” What would starting differently look like?
Think of a goal like “get organized.” What is one specific behavior that would make life more organized?
Think of a goal like “take better care of myself.” What would that look like in an ordinary day?
Think of a goal like “have better boundaries.” What is one behavior that would show the boundary exists?
Think of a goal like “communicate better.” What would you say or do differently?
Think of a goal like “handle my emotions better.” What action would you want to take differently during the next difficult moment?
Think of a goal like “be less hard on myself.” What would you actually do after the next mistake?
Think of a goal like “put myself first more.” What is one decision that would look different?
Think of a goal like “be more independent.” What is one thing you could take more ownership of?
Think of a goal like “ask for help more.” What is one thing you could ask for?
Think of a goal like “get out more.” What specific activity could happen?
Think of a goal like “try new things.” What is one new thing small enough to actually try?
Think of a goal like “take more risks.” What is one reasonable risk worth taking?
Think of a goal like “be myself more.” What behavior would be different?
Think of something you want to change. What action is entirely within your control?
Think of something you want to change. What is the smallest action that would still matter?
Think of something you want to change. What is most likely to interfere?
Think of something you want to change. What will you do when that barrier appears?
Think of something you want to change. What could make the desired action easier?
Think of something you want to change. What could make the old pattern harder?
Think of something you want to change. What reminder would appear at the right moment?
Think of something you want to change. What support would actually help?
Think of something you want to change. What is your rough-day version of the plan?
Think of something you want to change. How will you restart after a missed day?
Think of something you want to change. How will you know the plan is working?
Think of something you want to change. When would it make sense to adjust the plan?
Think of something you want to change. What would count as progress even if the outcome isn't perfect?

promptDecks.title: Do It Anyway
promptDecks.description: Description:** Helps clients practice taking meaningful action even when motivation, confidence, certainty, or emotional readiness is missing, building the ability to move toward goals and values without waiting for thoughts or feelings to change first.

prompts.text: Think of something important you've been waiting to feel ready for. What would it look like to begin before you feel completely ready?
Think of something you've been waiting to feel motivated to do. What could you do even if motivation doesn't show up first?
Think of something you've been waiting to feel confident about. What action could happen while confidence is still low?
Think of something you've been waiting to stop worrying about before doing. Could the worry come with you?
Think of something you've been waiting to feel less afraid of. What could you do while still feeling afraid?
Think of something you've been waiting to feel comfortable with. Does comfort need to come before action?
Think of something you've been waiting to feel certain about. What could you do without having a guarantee?
Think of something you've been waiting to understand completely. What can you do with what you know now?
Think of something you've been waiting to have more energy for. What version fits the energy you actually have?
Think of something you've been waiting for the “right time” to do. What makes now imperfect?
Think of something you've been waiting for circumstances to improve before starting. Is there any part that can happen under current circumstances?
Think of something you keep saying you'll do when you “feel better.” What happens if feeling better takes longer than you hope?
Think of something you know matters to you even though you don't currently feel like doing it.
Think of something your feelings say “no” to but your values say matters.
Think of something your anxiety wants you to avoid but another part of you wants to experience.
Think of something sadness makes feel pointless that still matters to you.
Think of something discouragement makes you want to quit that you still care about.
Think of something embarrassment makes you want to hide from that might still be worth facing.
Think of something insecurity makes you want to avoid. What would you choose if insecurity didn't make the decision?
Think of something uncertainty makes you want to postpone. What decision could you make without knowing exactly how it will turn out?
Think of something perfectionism makes difficult to begin. What could you do imperfectly?
Think of something self doubt makes you hesitate to try. What would trying look like without first proving you can succeed?
Think of something you're afraid to fail at. Could success for now be **doing it**, rather than succeeding at it?
Think of something you're afraid to do badly. What would it look like to let yourself be inexperienced?
Think of something you're afraid to do because other people might notice your nervousness. Could you participate while looking nervous?
Think of something you're afraid to say because your voice might shake, your face might change, or you might not say it perfectly. Could you say it anyway?
Think of something you want to ask for but feel nervous about. What matters more: feeling comfortable or giving yourself the chance to ask?
Think of a question you're afraid to ask because you might sound confused. Could being confused and asking the question happen together?
Think of something you're afraid to admit you don't know. What could you say anyway?
Think of something you want to tell someone but keep waiting for the perfect wording. What would a good enough version sound like?
Think of a conversation you're waiting to feel prepared for. How prepared do you realistically need to be?
Think of a conversation you're afraid will be uncomfortable. Could discomfort be part of having an important conversation?
Think of a boundary you're waiting to feel confident enough to set. Could you set it while feeling guilty or uncertain?
Think of something you want to say no to. Could you say no even if part of you wishes the other person wouldn't be disappointed?
Think of something you want to say yes to but fear keeps stopping you. What risk would you be accepting by saying yes?
Think of an opinion you want to express. Could you express it without knowing whether anyone will agree?
Think of something you need to advocate for. Could you speak up without knowing how the other person will respond?
Think of something you want someone to understand. Could you explain yourself without requiring them to understand perfectly?
Think of something important you want to communicate. Could you say it even if the conversation doesn't go exactly as planned?
Think of someone you want to reach out to. Could you send the message without knowing what they'll say back?
Think of someone you miss. What could you do without knowing whether they feel exactly the same way?
Think of someone you'd like to know better. Could you initiate connection without knowing whether a friendship will develop?
Think of a social situation you're tempted to avoid. Could you show up without requiring yourself to be outgoing?
Think of a group you're nervous to join. Could you participate without needing to feel like you belong immediately?
Think of somewhere you want to go but worry you'll feel awkward. Could feeling awkward be allowed?
Think of a social event where you feel pressure to have fun. Could the goal simply be to attend?
Think of a social situation where you feel pressure to be interesting. Could you show up without performing?
Think of a social situation where you feel pressure to say the right thing. Could you let yourself have an ordinary conversation?
Think of a social situation where you might not know what to say. Could you tolerate a little silence?
Think of a social situation where you might be judged. Could someone else's judgment exist without deciding what you do?
Think of something you're afraid people might think is weird. How important is doing what matters to you compared with avoiding that possibility?
Think of something you've stopped yourself from doing because “people might think...” What would you do if you stopped trying to control their thoughts?
Think of something you want to wear, say, try, make, share, or enjoy that self consciousness gets in the way of.
Think of something you enjoy but feel embarrassed about enjoying. Could you allow yourself to like it anyway?
Think of something authentic about yourself you hide because you're afraid of judgment. What is one small way to act more like yourself?
Think of something you care about that isn't considered impressive. Could it matter because **you** care about it?
Think of something you want to try even though you may not be naturally good at it.
Think of something you'd like to learn. Could you start as a beginner without needing evidence that you'll eventually excel?
Think of something you quit quickly when you're not immediately good at it. What would staying a beginner a little longer look like?
Think of something frustrating to practice. Could you practice while frustrated?
Think of something difficult to learn. Could confusion be part of learning rather than a signal to stop?
Think of something that makes you feel incompetent while you're learning it. Could that feeling exist without defining your actual ability?
Think of something you want to improve but hate making mistakes at. Could mistakes be part of the price of improvement?
Think of something you keep avoiding because you don't want to see yourself struggle. What might struggling teach you?
Think of something you want to attempt where failure is genuinely possible. Why might the attempt still matter?
Think of something where success isn't guaranteed. Does uncertainty about success make the effort meaningless?
Think of a goal where you keep asking, “What if I fail?” What happens if you also ask, “What if I never try?”
Think of something you want to do where you can't know whether the effort will pay off. What makes it worth trying anyway?
Think of something where you wish someone could promise you'll succeed. What could guide you when nobody can give that promise?
Think of something where fear of regret keeps you from choosing. Which regret would be harder: trying and regretting it, or never finding out?
Think of a decision where you're waiting to know which choice is definitely right. Could you choose the best option you can and adjust later?
Think of a decision where neither option feels completely safe. What matters enough to guide you despite the uncertainty?
Think of a choice where your brain wants to eliminate all risk. What would **reasonable** risk look like?
Think of a choice where waiting also has consequences. What are you choosing by not choosing?
Think of a change you're considering. What happens if nothing changes?
Think of a change you're considering that feels scary. Could fear mean the change matters rather than that it's wrong?
Think of something new where you can't predict how you'll feel afterward. Could you learn by experiencing it rather than solving it beforehand?
Think of an opportunity you're tempted to turn down because of anxiety. What would anxiety be deciding for you?
Think of an opportunity you're tempted to turn down because you might not be good enough. Do you need to be good enough before you begin?
Think of an opportunity you want but feel undeserving of. Could you let the person or process offering the opportunity decide whether you qualify?
Think of something you're afraid to apply for because you might not get it. What does not applying guarantee?
Think of something you're afraid to audition, interview, submit, or compete for. Could rejection be one possible outcome without making the attempt a mistake?
Think of something you'd like to create but are afraid won't be good. Could it exist before it is good?
Think of something you'd like to share but are afraid people won't like. Could sharing have value beyond approval?
Think of something you've been editing, fixing, or preparing because it doesn't feel ready. What would happen if you allowed it to be finished?
Think of something you're waiting to perfect before anyone sees it. What could you learn from letting it be seen earlier?
Think of something you want to start but feel like you need a complete plan first. What is enough planning to begin?
Think of something you're researching instead of doing. What do you already know enough to try?
Think of something you're organizing before starting. Is the organizing helping you begin or helping you postpone beginning?
Think of something you're planning repeatedly. What action would turn planning into doing?
Think of something you're thinking about doing more than you're actually doing. What is the smallest action that would change that?
Think of something where thinking about it feels safer than doing it. What information can action provide that thinking cannot?
Think of something you keep mentally rehearsing. What would happen if you let the real situation give you the next line?
Think of a conversation you keep replaying before it happens. Could you prepare the main point and let the rest unfold?
Think of something where you want to know how you'll handle every possible outcome. Could you trust yourself to respond when the outcome actually happens?
Think of something where your brain says, “But what if something goes wrong?” Could you deal with the problem **if** it appears rather than solving it now?
Think of something where uncertainty makes you freeze. What action doesn't require resolving the uncertainty?
Think of something where your brain wants one more piece of reassurance. What could you do before asking for it?
Think of something where you want someone to tell you that you're making the right choice. Could you make the choice while still wanting reassurance?
Think of a low stakes decision where you usually ask someone else what to do. Could you choose for yourself and tolerate wondering afterward?
Think of a decision you repeatedly reopen. Could you keep the decision even while doubt remains?
Think of something you repeatedly check before moving on. Could you move on without achieving the feeling of complete certainty?
Think of something you redo until it feels right. Could you stop while it still feels slightly unfinished?
Think of something you prepare excessively for. Could you stop once preparation is reasonable rather than once anxiety disappears?
Think of something you avoid because anxiety tells you you're not safe. What evidence tells you whether the situation is actually unsafe or merely uncomfortable?
Think of something safe that your body reacts to as dangerous. Could you allow the alarm to be present without automatically obeying it?
Think of a situation where your heart races, your stomach hurts, you shake, sweat, blush, or feel other anxiety sensations. Could you continue while your body does that?
Think of something where anxiety makes you want to escape. What would staying a little longer teach you?
Think of something where anxiety makes you want to cancel. What could you learn by going despite the anxiety?
Think of something where anxiety says, “Leave.” What would **you** choose if anxiety were allowed to speak but not decide?
Think of something where anxiety says, “Don't do it.” What other voice deserves a vote?
Think of something where your body says, “I can't.” How could you distinguish “I can't” from “I really don't want to feel this”?
Think of a feeling you usually treat as a stop sign. Could it become information rather than an instruction?
Think of sadness that tells you to withdraw. What action might support you even if withdrawal feels easier?
Think of low mood that tells you nothing will be enjoyable. Could you do something without demanding enjoyment?
Think of low mood that tells you there's no point. What could matter even if it doesn't change your mood immediately?
Think of low mood that tells you to stay in bed or isolate. What one action could keep you connected to the day?
Think of numbness that makes everything feel meaningless. Could you act according to what **usually** matters to you even while you can't feel it strongly?
Think of hopelessness that says nothing will change. Do you need to believe things will improve before taking one useful action?
Think of a moment when you can't access hope. What could guide you besides hope?
Think of a moment when the future feels empty. Could you make a decision based only on what matters for the next hour or day?
Think of a moment when you feel like giving up on a goal. Could you delay the decision to quit until the feeling changes?
Think of a moment when you're exhausted by trying. Would a smaller step be different from giving up?
Think of a moment when continuing the original plan isn't realistic. Could adjusting the plan be a form of continuing?
Think of something you need to do while feeling sad. What version is realistic without expecting yourself to function exactly as usual?
Think of something you need to do while feeling anxious. What could you accomplish without needing the anxiety to disappear?
Think of something you need to do while feeling angry. What action fits your goals even if anger remains?
Think of something you need to do while feeling embarrassed. What would moving forward look like while the embarrassment is still there?
Think of something you need to do while feeling disappointed. What does disappointment not prevent you from doing?
Think of something you need to do while feeling insecure. What could you do without first proving that you're good enough?
Think of something you need to do while feeling overwhelmed. What is small enough to do inside the overwhelm?
Think of something you need to do while feeling tired. What is the minimum effective version?
Think of something you don't feel like doing but usually appreciate afterward. What makes starting worth it?
Think of something that almost never sounds appealing before you start but often feels worthwhile afterward.
Think of something where anticipation is worse than the actual activity. What does that tell you about letting anticipation decide?
Think of something where your motivation tends to increase once you begin. What could help you reach the beginning?
Think of something where action changes your mood more reliably than thinking about changing your mood.
Think of something you do consistently even when you don't feel like doing it. What allows you to act without motivation there?
Think of an area where you've learned not to debate with yourself every time. What could you borrow from that approach?
Think of something where having a routine helps you act regardless of mood.
Think of something where deciding ahead of time would prevent your current feelings from making the whole decision.
Think of something important you frequently cancel based on how you feel in the moment. Would deciding ahead of time change anything?
Think of something where “I'll see how I feel” usually means you won't do it. What could you decide instead?
Think of something where flexibility is appropriate. How can you tell the difference between adjusting the plan and avoiding the plan?
Think of something where resting is genuinely the effective choice. How do you know when **not** doing something is aligned with your needs rather than avoidance?
Think of something where pushing through would be harmful. What makes choosing not to do it different from fear making the choice?
Think of a situation where “do it anyway” would **not** be appropriate because the action is unsafe, harmful, or violates an important boundary.
Think of something where listening to discomfort protects you. How is that different from discomfort simply being unpleasant?
Think of something where you need to respect a physical or emotional limit. Could honoring a real limit still involve making an intentional choice?
Think of something where your goal isn't to force yourself but to stop requiring a particular feeling before you act.
Think of something where you can choose an action **with** your feelings rather than against them.
Imagine someone says, “I'll go when I'm not anxious anymore.” What could keep them waiting?
Imagine someone says, “I'll apply when I feel confident.” How might confidence actually develop?
Imagine someone says, “I'll start when I'm motivated.” What could happen if action is what creates motivation?
Imagine someone says, “I'll say something when I know exactly what to say.” How long might they stay silent?
Imagine someone says, “I'll make a decision once I'm completely sure.” What happens when certainty isn't available?
Imagine someone says, “I'll set the boundary when I stop feeling guilty.” Could guilt continue even when the boundary is healthy?
Imagine someone says, “I'll try once I know I won't fail.” What does that rule prevent?
Imagine someone says, “I'll go when I know I won't feel awkward.” Could awkwardness be survivable?
Imagine someone says, “I'll reach out when I know they want to hear from me.” How could they ever find out without reaching out?
Imagine someone says, “I'll do something fun when I feel less depressed.” What could happen to their opportunities for pleasure and connection while they wait?
Imagine someone says, “I'll get out of bed when I have energy.” Could getting up affect energy?
Imagine someone says, “I'll stop avoiding when the fear gets smaller.” What could help fear get smaller if avoidance continues?
Imagine someone says, “I'll speak up when I'm brave enough.” Could speaking up itself be the brave act?
Imagine someone says, “I'll be myself once I know people will accept me.” Is that certainty available?
Imagine someone says, “I'll make the change when it feels easier.” Could beginning be part of what eventually makes it easier?
Imagine someone does something important while feeling anxious the entire time. Did they fail because the anxiety stayed?
Imagine someone attends an event but doesn't enjoy it much. Could showing up still be progress?
Imagine someone sets a boundary and feels guilty afterward. Could the boundary still have been appropriate?
Imagine someone asks for something and gets rejected. Could asking still have been a meaningful action?
Imagine someone tries something and fails. Could doing it anyway still have taught them something valuable?
Imagine someone starts a task with no motivation and only completes ten minutes. Could those ten minutes count?
Imagine someone takes a small step while still feeling hopeless. What might the action represent even if hope doesn't immediately increase?
What feelings do you most often require yourself to have before acting?
Which feeling do you most often wait to disappear before acting?
What does waiting for the “right feeling” cost you?
Which emotions tend to get too much decision making power in your life?
When does anxiety get to choose for you?
When does guilt get to choose for you?
When does embarrassment get to choose for you?
When does insecurity get to choose for you?
When does low motivation get to choose for you?
When does perfectionism get to choose for you?
When does uncertainty get to choose for you?
When does fear of disappointing people get to choose for you?
What decisions would look different if feelings were allowed to give information but not make the final choice?
How can you respect a feeling without obeying every urge it creates?
How can you validate “I really don't want to do this” without automatically deciding not to do it?
Can you dread something and still choose it?
Can you dislike something and still decide it's worth doing?
Can you be uncertain and still choose?
Can you be scared and still approach?
Can you feel awkward and still participate?
Can you feel embarrassed and still recover?
Can you feel guilty and still maintain a reasonable boundary?
Can you feel rejected and still reach toward connection again?
Can you feel discouraged and still take another step?
Can you feel unmotivated and still begin?
Can you feel tired and still choose a very small action?
Can you feel overwhelmed and still do one thing?
Can you feel sad and still care for yourself?
Can you feel numb and still act according to what matters?
Can you feel hopeless and still postpone giving up?
Can you have a thought without agreeing with it?
Can you have a prediction without letting it determine your behavior?
Can you have doubt without solving it?
Can you have an urge without acting on it?
Can you have fear without making fear the decision maker?
What is the difference between **feeling ready** and **being able to take one step**?
What is the difference between confidence and willingness?
What is the difference between motivation and commitment?
What is the difference between comfort and safety?
What is the difference between uncertainty and danger?
What is the difference between not wanting to do something and deciding it isn't worth doing?
What is the difference between honoring a limit and avoiding discomfort?
What is the difference between forcing yourself and intentionally choosing something difficult?
What is the difference between “I shouldn't feel this way” and “I can feel this way and still choose what I do”?
What makes an uncomfortable action worth doing?

What is something you've already done despite being afraid?
What is something you've already done despite not feeling confident?
What is something you've already done despite not feeling ready?
What is something you've already done despite not feeling motivated?
What is something you've already done despite uncertainty?

Think of a time you were nervous and went anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you were unmotivated and started anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you felt awkward and stayed anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you doubted yourself and tried anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you expected failure and tried anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you were afraid someone would say no and asked anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you were afraid of disappointing someone and spoke honestly anyway. What happened?
Think of a time you didn't know whether a decision was right and made the best choice you could anyway.
Think of a time you acted according to what mattered even though it felt terrible in the moment.

promptDecks.title: Emotional Regulation
promptDecks.description: Helps clients understand their emotions, recognize triggers and patterns, and build skills for responding to intense feelings in ways that are effective and aligned with their goals.

promptDecks.title: Core Beliefs
promptDecks.description: Helps clients identify deeper beliefs they hold about themselves, other people, and the world, explore how those beliefs shape thoughts and behavior, and examine whether long standing conclusions still fit their current experiences.

prompts.text: Think of a negative thought you have about yourself often. What deeper belief might be underneath it?
Think of something that tends to make you feel not good enough. What does your mind say that situation proves about you?
Think of a mistake that feels especially painful. What does making that mistake seem to mean about who you are?
Think of a criticism that's difficult for you to hear. What belief about yourself does it seem to confirm?
Think of a compliment that's difficult for you to believe. What belief about yourself makes the compliment hard to accept?
Think of something you feel you constantly need to prove. What are you afraid would be true if you stopped proving it?
Think of something you work especially hard to hide from other people. What are you afraid they would think if they saw it?

Think of a relationship where you keep your guard up. What does your guard protect you from believing or feeling?
Think of a relationship where closeness feels uncomfortable. What does being known by someone seem to risk?
Think of a relationship where you pull away when you start caring. What might distance protect you from?
Think of a relationship where you tolerate things you don't want to tolerate. What belief makes leaving, speaking up, or setting a boundary difficult?
Think of a time someone treated you badly. What did you conclude about yourself because of how they treated you?
Think of something that happened to you that you once interpreted as evidence about your worth. Does another person's behavior actually determine your worth?
Think of a painful experience that shaped how you see yourself. What conclusion did you make about yourself at the time?
Think of a painful experience that shaped how you see other people. What conclusion did you make about people?
Think of a painful experience that shaped how you see the world. What conclusion did you make about how safe, fair, or predictable life is?
Think of something you learned about yourself when you were younger. Who or what taught you that?
Think of a message about yourself that you've carried for years. Where did the message begin?
Think of something another person repeatedly said about you. Did repetition make it feel like a fact?
Think of a label you were given when you were younger. How much does that label still influence how you see yourself?
Think of a role you had in your family or another group. What did that role teach you that you were supposed to be?
Think of something you learned you needed to do to receive approval, attention, safety, or connection.
Think of something you learned not to do because of how other people responded.
Think of an emotion you learned to hide. What did you learn might happen if you showed it?
Think of a need you learned not to express. What did you learn about having that need?
Think of something you learned about making mistakes. What were mistakes treated as meaning?
Think of something you learned about achievement. What did success seem to earn you?
Think of something you learned about failure. What did failure seem to cost you?
Think of something you learned about asking for help. What happened when people needed support?
Think of something you learned about conflict. Did conflict mean disagreement, danger, rejection, punishment, or something else?
Think of something you learned about trust. What experiences taught you that lesson?
Think of something you learned about depending on people. What did your experiences teach you to expect?
Think of something you learned about being vulnerable. What seemed to happen when people showed vulnerability?
Think of something you learned about being different. What messages did you receive about fitting in?
Think of something you learned about being yourself around other people. When did it feel safe, and when didn't it?
Think of a belief you have about yourself that feels more like a fact than an opinion. What makes it feel so certain?
Think of a belief that begins with “I am...” How long have you believed it?
Think of a belief that begins with “I'm not...” What experiences does your brain use as evidence?
Think of a belief that begins with “I'm too...” What does “too” mean, and according to whom?
Think of a belief that begins with “I'm not enough...” Enough for what?

Think of a belief that begins with “People always...” What experiences taught you to expect that?

Think of a belief that begins with “I have to...” What are you afraid would happen if you didn't?
Think of a belief that begins with “I can't let people...” What are you protecting yourself from?
Think of a belief that begins with “I should be...” Where did that standard come from?

Think of a belief that begins with “To be good enough, I need to...” Who decided that requirement?
Think of a belief that says your worth depends on achievement. What happens to your sense of worth when you struggle?
Think of a belief that says your worth depends on being liked. What happens when someone doesn't like you?
Think of a belief that says your worth depends on being needed. What happens when someone doesn't need your help?
Think of a belief that says your worth depends on being easy, agreeable, or low maintenance. What happens when you have needs?
Think of a belief that says your worth depends on being strong. What happens when you need support?
Think of a belief that says you must be perfect to avoid criticism. Has perfection ever actually guaranteed that?
Think of a belief that says mistakes make you less worthy. Would you apply that same rule to someone you care about?
Think of a belief that says struggling means you're weak. What evidence from your life complicates that belief?
Think of a belief that says needing help means you're incapable. What examples challenge that conclusion?
Think of a belief that says being rejected means you're unlovable. Does one person's choice have enough information to establish that?
Think of a belief that says being left means you weren't enough. What other factors can affect why relationships change or end?
Think of a belief that says conflict means someone will leave. What experiences do you have where relationships survived disagreement?
Think of a belief that says you can't trust anyone. Are there different levels of trust rather than only total trust or no trust?
Think of a belief that says other people will eventually hurt you. Does protecting yourself from every possibility of hurt have costs too?
Think of a belief that says the world is unsafe. Where is caution useful, and where might the belief be applying danger too broadly?
Think of a belief that says you have no control. What choices, even small ones, remain available to you?
Think of a belief that says nothing you do matters. What evidence might be easy to overlook when that belief is active?
Think of a belief that says things never get better. What changes in your life would that belief have failed to predict?
Think of a belief that says you always mess things up. What examples don't fit “always”?
Think of a belief that says you aren't capable. What have you learned, handled, survived, or figured out that doesn't fit?
Think of a belief that says you're weak. What has required strength from you?
Think of a belief that says you're a failure. What does that label leave out?
Think of a belief that says you're unlikeable. Who has enjoyed, valued, cared about, or chosen connection with you?
Think of a belief that says you're unwanted. What experiences don't fit that story?
Think of a belief that says you're a burden. What is the difference between having needs and being a burden?
Think of a belief that says you're selfish. Could having boundaries or needs exist alongside caring deeply about other people?
Think of a belief that says you're “too much.” In what relationships or environments have you not felt like too much?
Think of a belief that says you're “not enough.” What parts of yourself are being excluded from that judgment?
Think of a belief that says something is fundamentally wrong with you. What would you need to know about a whole person before making a conclusion that large?
Think of a belief that developed during a difficult period. Could it have helped you make sense of what was happening at the time?
Think of a belief that may once have protected you. Is it still protecting you now, or is it limiting you?
Think of a belief that made sense in one environment. Does the same rule apply everywhere?
Think of a belief you developed around one person. Has your brain started applying it to everyone?
Think of a belief based on several painful experiences. What experiences have occurred since then that don't fit it?
Think of a belief that feels old. How old do you feel when that belief gets activated?
Think of a belief that sounds like someone else's voice. Whose voice does it resemble?
Think of a belief you inherited rather than consciously chose. Do you still agree with it?
Think of a belief you've never really questioned. What would happen if you treated it as a hypothesis rather than a fact?
If your belief were on trial, what evidence would support it?
If your belief were on trial, what evidence would challenge it?
What evidence does your belief tend to notice immediately?
What evidence does your belief tend to dismiss?
When something fits your belief, how strongly do you remember it?
When something contradicts your belief, how does your brain explain it away?
What experiences would you expect to see if your belief were completely true?
Do those experiences actually happen every time?
What would someone who knows you well say about this belief?
What would someone who cares about you notice that the belief leaves out?
What would you say if someone you cared about believed the same thing about themselves?
Would you require the same amount of evidence before believing something this negative about another person?
What evidence from the last year supports a different view of yourself?
What evidence from your current life might be more relevant than evidence from years ago?
What has changed about you since this belief first developed?
What has changed about your environment since this belief first developed?
What abilities do you have now that you didn't have when the belief began?
What relationships do you have now that challenge what earlier relationships taught you?
What choices do you have now that you may not have had before?
What is one experience that doesn't fit your old belief?
What is one exception your belief has trouble explaining?
What is one strength your belief consistently leaves out?
What is one piece of positive evidence you usually dismiss?
What would happen if that evidence counted just as much as negative evidence?
What would a more complete belief about yourself sound like?
How could you make the belief more specific instead of applying it to your entire identity?
How could you replace “I am...” with a statement about what you sometimes feel, think, struggle with, or do?
Instead of “I'm a failure,” what statement would describe your actual experiences more accurately?
Instead of “I'm unlovable,” what statement could acknowledge relationship pain without defining your worth?

Instead of “Nothing will change,” what belief could make room for not knowing what happens next?
What is a belief about yourself you would like to develop?
What evidence already exists for that new belief?
What small action could help you gather more evidence for it?
What would you notice differently if you believed it 10% more?
How might you behave differently if you believed it 10% more?
What could you try that your old belief usually stops you from trying?
What relationship behavior might change if your old belief had less control?
What boundary might become easier?
What risk might become worth taking?
What support might become easier to accept?
What mistake might become easier to recover from?
What part of yourself might become easier to show?
What experience could give your brain new information?
What belief about yourself has your life already started disproving?
What old belief are you ready to question rather than automatically obey?
What would you want to believe about yourself instead?
What would a belief that is realistic, compassionate, and flexible sound like?
What is one piece of evidence you want to remember the next time the old belief shows up?

promptDecks.title: Notice
promptDecks.description: Helps clients slow down and notice their thoughts, feelings, body sensations, and surroundings with curiosity and without immediately needing to react or change them.

prompts.text: What do you see right now?
Find three things you can see right now.
Find something red.
Find something blue.
Find something green.
Find something yellow.
Find something with more than one color.
Find the brightest thing you can see.
Find the darkest thing you can see.
Find something shiny.
Find something transparent.
Find something tiny.
Find something bigger than you.
Find something smaller than your hand.
Find something round.
Find something with straight lines.
Find something with an interesting shape.
Find something with a pattern.
Find something that looks soft.
Find something that looks rough.
Find something moving.
Find something completely still.
Find something close to you.
Find something far away.
Find something you hadn't noticed until right now.
Look around and find five different colors.
Look around and find three different shapes.
Choose one object and notice three details about it.
Choose an ordinary object and look for something you've never noticed about it.
Look at one object for ten seconds. What do you notice?
What is the most interesting thing you can see from where you are?
What is the smallest detail you can find in the room?
What do you hear right now?
Find three sounds you can hear right now.
Listen for the quietest sound you can hear.
Listen for the loudest sound you can hear.
Listen for a sound close to you.
Listen for a sound far away.
Listen for a sound in front of you.
Listen for a sound behind you.
Listen for a sound above you.
Listen for a sound outside the room.
Can you hear something repeating?
Can you hear a sound that comes and goes?
Can you hear a sound you usually ignore?
Close your eyes for a moment. What sound becomes easier to notice?
Listen quietly for ten seconds. How many different sounds can you find?
Choose one sound and follow it until it stops.
What is the most pleasant sound you can hear right now?
What can you touch right now?
Find something soft.
Find something hard.
Find something smooth.
Find something rough.
Find something bumpy.
Find something squishy.
Find something fuzzy.
Find something cool.
Find something warm.
Find something with an interesting texture.
Touch two different things. How do they feel different?
Hold something in your hand and notice its weight.
Hold something and notice its temperature.
Run one finger across a surface slowly. What do you notice?
Notice how your clothing feels against your skin.
Notice what your feet are touching.
Notice what your hands are touching.
Notice where your body touches the chair, couch, or floor.
Press your feet into the ground and notice the pressure.
Press your palms together and notice what you feel.
Rub your fingertips together slowly. What do you notice?
Wiggle your toes and notice what you feel.
What can you smell right now?
Can you find a smell you didn't notice at first?
Choose one smell and describe it without naming what it comes from.
Does the air have a smell right now?
Does anything nearby have a familiar smell?
What does a smell in the room remind you of?
Take one slow breath through your nose. What do you notice?
What taste do you notice in your mouth right now?
Take a sip of water and notice the temperature.
Take a sip of water and notice how it feels in your mouth.
If you have something to eat, take one bite slowly and notice the texture.
If you have something to eat, notice when the flavor first appears.
If you have something to eat, notice whether the flavor changes while you chew.
Take one slow breath and notice where you feel it.
Notice the air entering your nose.
Notice the air leaving your nose.
Notice whether your inhale and exhale feel different.
Take three breaths and count each one.
Take one ordinary breath without changing it. What do you notice?
Breathe out slowly and notice what your body does.
Take a slow breath and notice whether anything changes.
Notice your hands without moving them.
Notice your feet without moving them.
Notice your face without changing your expression.
Notice your shoulders without trying to relax them.
Notice your jaw without trying to change it.
Notice your posture right now.
Notice whether your body is moving or still.
Sit completely still for five seconds. What do you notice?
Move as slowly as you can for five seconds. What do you notice?
Stretch your arms and notice what changes.
Stretch your legs and notice what changes.
Squeeze your hands and slowly let go. What do you notice?
Roll your shoulders once and notice the movement.
Turn your head slowly from side to side and notice what changes in your view.
Wiggle your fingers slowly and watch them move.
Move one hand as slowly as you possibly can.
Tap your fingers one at a time and notice each tap.
Notice one thing outside your body.
Now notice one thing inside your body.
Switch your attention between a sound and something you can see.
Switch your attention between your feet and something across the room.
Notice something close to you, then something far away.
Notice something still, then something moving.
Notice something you can hear, then something you can touch.
Notice one thing with each of your senses.
Find five things you can see, four things you can touch, three things you can hear, two things you can smell, and one thing you can taste.
Choose one object and notice its color, shape, texture, and temperature.
Look around slowly from left to right. What did you notice?
Look around the room as if you've never been here before. What stands out?
Pretend you're a detective. Find three details that would be easy to miss.
Pretend you're taking a photograph with your eyes. What would be in the picture?
Pretend you're an alien seeing this room for the first time. What would seem interesting?
Find something you've seen many times and notice one new detail.
Pick one ordinary object and describe it without saying its name.
Find something that makes you curious.
Find something that makes you smile.
Find something that feels comforting to look at.
Find something that reminds you where you are right now.
Name three things that tell you where you are right now.
Name the place you're in, the day, and what you're doing right now.
Notice what is happening right now instead of what happened before or might happen later.
What's one thing happening right this second?
What's one thing you can notice without needing to change it?
Can you notice something uncomfortable without immediately trying to fix it?
Can you notice something pleasant without rushing past it?
Choose one sensation and watch what happens to it for ten seconds.
Does the sensation stay the same, get stronger, get weaker, move, or disappear?
Choose one sound and notice its beginning, middle, and end.
Choose one breath and follow it from beginning to end.
Notice one thing your attention keeps returning to.
Where did your attention go when you weren't trying to control it?
Bring your attention back to one thing you can see.
Bring your attention back to one sound.
Bring your attention back to your feet.
Bring your attention back to your breathing.
What is easiest to notice right now?
What is hardest to notice right now?
What did you notice that you weren't aware of a minute ago?
What changed when you started paying attention?
What's one thing you can notice right now that reminds you you're here?

promptDecks.title: Cognitive Defusion
promptDecks.description: Build distance from difficult thoughts by noticing them as mental events rather than facts, commands, or problems that must be solved before moving forward.

prompts.text: What thoughts tend to get stuck in your mind?
What thought has been showing up a lot lately?
What thoughts are hardest for you to let pass?
What thoughts tend to pull your attention away from what you are doing?
What thoughts become louder when you are stressed?
What thoughts show up when you are anxious?
What thoughts show up when you are upset with yourself?
What thoughts show up when something does not go the way you hoped?
What thoughts tend to show up before you avoid something?
What thoughts tend to show up when you are trying something new?
What does your mind say when it thinks something might go wrong?
What does your mind say when you make a mistake?
What does your mind say when you feel uncertain?
What does your mind say when you are worried about what other people think?
What does your mind say when you compare yourself to someone else?
What does your mind say when you are about to do something difficult?
How can you tell when you are caught up in a thought?

What happens to your emotions when you believe a difficult thought completely?
What happens to your behavior when you believe everything your mind tells you?
What do you tend to do when a difficult thought feels completely true?
How does a thought change when you notice it instead of automatically believing it?
What is the difference between having a thought and knowing something is true?
How can you tell the difference between a thought, a feeling, and a fact?
Does thinking something make it true?
Can a thought feel true without being a fact?
Can your mind be convincing and still be wrong?
What is something your mind has predicted that did not happen?
What is something you once believed strongly that you see differently now?
What is a thought that changes depending on your mood?
What is a thought that feels more believable when you are tired or stressed?
What does that tell you about how reliable thoughts can be?
What happens when you treat every thought like an instruction?
What happens when you treat every thought like something you have to solve?
Which thoughts tend to boss you around?
What does your mind tell you that you “have to” do?
What does your mind tell you that you “cannot” do?
What does your mind tell you that you “should” be like?
What rules does your mind create for you?
What happens when your mind says you need to feel ready before doing something?
What happens when your mind says you need to be certain before making a decision?
What happens when your mind says you need to stop feeling anxious before doing something important?
What happens when your mind says you need to do something perfectly?
What does listening to those rules cost you?
What does your mind try to protect you from?
When is your mind trying to help but making things harder?
What thought seems protective but keeps you from something important?
What does worry promise it will do for you?
Does worrying more always make you more prepared?
What does overthinking promise to help you figure out?
Does thinking about something longer always make the answer clearer?
What does self criticism seem to be trying to accomplish?
Does being hard on yourself actually help you become the person you want to be?
What does avoidance promise will happen if you listen to it?
What happens in the long run when you follow an avoidant thought?
What is your mind trying to prevent when it tells you not to take a risk?
What might your mind be trying to protect when it tells you other people will judge you?
What is the difference between your mind trying to protect you and your mind knowing what will happen?
What changes when you see a difficult thought as your brain trying to protect you?
What would happen if you did not have to argue with every difficult thought?
What would happen if you let a thought be there without trying to prove it wrong?
What would happen if you stopped trying to make a thought disappear?
What thoughts become stronger when you try not to think about them?
What happens when you tell yourself you absolutely cannot think about something?
What might change if getting rid of the thought were no longer the goal?
Can you dislike a thought without needing to get rid of it?
Can a difficult thought be present while you continue with your day?
Can you feel uncertain without solving the uncertainty?
Can you notice a scary thought without treating it like a warning?
Can you notice a self critical thought without agreeing with it?
Can you notice an urge without acting on it?
Can you have the thought “I can't do this” and still try?
Can you have the thought “Something will go wrong” and still move forward?
Can you have the thought “They might judge me” and still be yourself?
Can you have the thought “I'm not ready” and take one small step anyway?
What is something important you could do while a difficult thought came along with you?
What would change if your thoughts did not have to disappear before you acted?
What is one thought you could practice noticing instead of fighting?
What happens when you add “I'm having the thought that…” before a difficult thought?
How does “I'm going to fail” feel different from “I'm having the thought that I'm going to fail”?
How does “Nobody likes me” feel different from “My mind is telling me that nobody likes me”?
What happens when you describe a thought as something your mind is producing?
What happens when you say “My mind is giving me the story that…”?
What happens when you thank your mind for a thought instead of arguing with it?
What might “Thanks, mind” help you remember?
What would it be like to say, “There goes my mind again” when a familiar thought appears?
What familiar story does your mind tell you over and over?
What title would you give a thought pattern that keeps returning?
What would you call the story your mind tells when you are afraid of failing?
What would you call the story your mind tells when you worry about being judged?
What would you call the story your mind tells when you feel like you are not good enough?
How does recognizing an old mental story change the way you respond to it?
What is a thought you have heard from your mind hundreds of times?
Does hearing a thought repeatedly make it more true?
What could you say when an old thought shows up again?
How could you acknowledge a thought without giving it control?
What does it feel like to notice, “My mind is doing that thing again”?
If your thoughts were notifications on your phone, which ones would you stop opening immediately?
If your thoughts were pop up ads, which ones would you notice without clicking?
If your thoughts were clouds, which thought could you watch pass by?
If your thoughts were leaves floating down a stream, which thought would you place on a leaf?
If your thoughts were cars passing on a road, what would it be like to watch them without chasing them?
If your thoughts were radio stations, which station does your mind tune into too often?
If your mind had a worry channel, what kinds of programs would it play?
If your mind had a self criticism channel, what would the announcer sound like?
If a difficult thought were background music, what could you keep doing while it played?
If your thoughts were passengers on a bus, which passenger tends to shout the loudest?
If a difficult thought came along for the ride without driving, where would you choose to go?
If your mind were an overprotective bodyguard, what would it warn you about?
If your mind were a nervous weather reporter, what predictions would it make?
If your mind were a storyteller, what story does it keep retelling?
If your mind were a salesperson, what idea would it keep trying to convince you to buy?
If a difficult thought were written on a T shirt, would wearing it make the words true?
If you wrote a difficult thought in silly handwriting, would its meaning change?
If you repeated a difficult word until it sounded strange, what would you notice?
If your most critical thought had a ridiculous voice, would it feel different?
If a familiar thought had a character, what would that character be like?
If your worry had to introduce itself as a thought instead of a fact, what would it say?
If your mind could put subtitles under its thoughts, what would the subtitle say?
If your brain could label a thought “prediction,” “memory,” “judgment,” or “worry,” which label would fit?
What label could help you recognize a thought without getting pulled into it?
What happens when you notice “judging” instead of focusing on the judgment itself?
What happens when you notice “worrying” instead of solving the worry?
What happens when you notice “comparing” instead of following the comparison?
What happens when you notice “remembering” instead of treating a memory like it is happening now?
