Think of a “should” you use against yourself. What happens if you replace “should” with “I'd like to,” “it would help to,” or “it's important to me to”?
Think of something you believe you “have to” do perfectly. What would a more flexible rule sound like?
Think of a standard you hold yourself to that you would never demand from someone else. How could you make the standard fairer?
Think of a situation where anything less than perfect feels like failure. What would a thought that allows for “good enough” sound like?
Think of something you did partly well and partly poorly. What thought can hold both parts at the same time?
Think of a day you've labeled a “terrible day.” What would a more accurate description include?
Think of a relationship you've labeled as completely good or completely bad. What would a more complete description sound like?
Think of a situation where two things can be true at once. How could your thought make room for both?
Think of something you don't like but can tolerate. How could you change “I can't stand this” into something more accurate?
Think of something that feels unbearable in the moment. What could you tell yourself that separates “this feels awful” from “I cannot get through it”?
Think of a feeling you wish would disappear. What thought could help you make room for the feeling without letting it decide what you do?
Think of a difficult emotion that makes you want to escape immediately. What could you tell yourself that helps you stay with it a little longer?
Think of something you're avoiding because you don't feel ready. What thought could allow you to act without needing to feel completely ready first?
Think of something you're waiting to feel confident enough to do. What could you tell yourself about acting while confidence is still catching up?
Think of something you're afraid to try. What thought would make taking one small step feel possible?
Think of something you might fail at. What thought would let failure be a possible outcome without making it a reason not to try?
Think of a situation where you want certainty before making a choice. What could you tell yourself about making the best decision you can with the information you have?
Think of something your anxious brain wants a guarantee about. What could you say instead of trying to give yourself a guarantee you can't actually have?
Think of a worry that keeps asking “What if?” What is a response that doesn't require you to solve every possible future problem?
Think of a situation where reassurance only helps for a little while. What could you tell yourself instead of trying to become 100% certain?
Think of a thought that sounds reassuring but you don't actually believe. How could you make it more believable?
Turn “Everything will be fine” into something you could believe even when you don't know how things will turn out.
Turn “There's nothing to worry about” into something that acknowledges the worry without feeding it.
Turn “I shouldn't feel this way” into a thought that makes room for the feeling.
Turn “I need to calm down” into a thought that doesn't make calmness a requirement.
Turn “I have to stop thinking about this” into a thought that allows the thought to exist without giving it all your attention.
Turn “I need to know what they think of me” into a thought that makes room for not knowing.
Turn “I need everyone to like me” into something more realistic and sustainable.
Turn “If they're upset with me, I did something wrong” into a thought that allows for other possibilities.
Turn “If I disappoint someone, I'm a bad person” into a thought that separates another person's feelings from your worth.
Turn “If I say no, they'll be mad at me” into a thought that acknowledges both the possibility and your right to have limits.
Turn “If I ask for help, they'll think I can't do it” into a more balanced thought.
Turn “If I make a mistake, everyone will notice” into a thought that leaves room for what you don't know.
Turn “If I fail, it means I'm not good enough” into a thought that separates an outcome from your identity.
Turn “I'm behind everyone else” into a thought that focuses on your own progress rather than an imagined timeline.
Turn “I should be better by now” into something that recognizes that change doesn't follow a perfect schedule.
Turn “I'm back at square one” into a thought that recognizes what you've learned even when you're struggling again.
Turn “Nothing has changed” into a thought that looks for small changes your brain might be overlooking.
Turn “I'll always feel like this” into something accurate about what you know right now.
Turn “There's no point” into a thought that leaves room for one small action still mattering.
Turn “I can't handle another bad thing happening” into a thought that draws on ways you've handled difficult things before.
Turn “This is too much” into a thought that helps you decide what the next manageable piece is.
Turn “I have to fix everything” into a thought that identifies what actually belongs to you.
Turn “I ruined everything” into a statement about what actually went wrong and what can still happen next.
Turn “Everyone is against me” into a thought that separates the people or situations actually involved from everyone else.
Turn “Nobody understands” into a thought that makes room for finding one person who might understand part of what you're experiencing.
Turn “I'm never going to get better at this” into a thought that reflects what learning and progress actually look like.
Turn “I can't do this” into a thought that would help you take the next step.
Take a thought that hurts but contains some truth. How could you keep the true part without adding unnecessary judgment or prediction?
Take a thought that sounds positive but feels fake. Rewrite it into something realistic enough that you could actually use it.
Take one of your most common difficult thoughts. What would a version that is fair, accurate, and useful sound like?
What is one balanced thought you would actually want available the next time things feel difficult?

promptDecks.title: Readiness
promptDecks.description:
Helps clients explore how ready they feel to make a change, what is influencing their current level of readiness, and what might help them move closer to taking action.

Use a 0–10 scale throughout: 0 = not ready at all, 10 = completely ready.

prompts.text: Think of one change you are considering. From 0–10, how ready are you to make that change?

promptDecks.title: Coping Thoughts
promptDecks.description: Helps clients develop realistic, believable thoughts they can use during difficult moments to tolerate emotions, respond more effectively, and keep moving forward without requiring themselves to feel better first.

prompts.text: Think of something difficult you're dealing with right now. What could you tell yourself that would help you get through the next part?
Think of a situation that feels overwhelming. What could you tell yourself to make the next step feel manageable?
Think of something that feels impossible right now. What could you tell yourself that acknowledges the difficulty without deciding you can't do it?
Think of something you don't know how to handle yet. What thought could remind you that you don't have to know everything immediately?
Think of a problem you can't solve right now. What could you tell yourself while you wait for more information?
Think of something you wish you could fix immediately. What thought could help you tolerate not having a solution yet?
Think of something outside your control. What could you tell yourself to redirect your attention toward what you can control?
Think of something you can't change. What thought could help you decide what to do from here?
Think of something that didn't go the way you wanted. What could you tell yourself that leaves room for a next step?

Think of a situation where waiting is difficult. What could you tell yourself to get through the waiting?
Think of a situation where you don't know what will happen. What thought could help you tolerate the uncertainty?
Think of something your brain wants certainty about. What could you tell yourself instead of trying to guarantee the outcome?

Think of something you've been putting off. What could you tell yourself that focuses only on starting?
Think of something that feels too big. What thought could bring your attention back to one piece?
Think of a task where you feel like you have to do everything. What could you tell yourself about doing enough for now?
Think of something you're struggling to finish. What thought could help you continue imperfectly?
Think of something where perfection is getting in the way of progress. What coping thought could give you permission to do it well enough?
Think of something you don't want to do badly. What could you tell yourself that allows you to be a beginner?
Think of something you're learning. What thought could help you tolerate not being good at it yet?

Think of something you wish you'd done differently. What could you tell yourself about what you can do now?

Think of a setback after you'd been doing better. What could you tell yourself so the setback doesn't become “I'm back at the beginning”?

Think of a moment when progress feels too slow. What thought could help you notice movement without demanding a perfect timeline?

Think of a day when you don't feel motivated. What thought could help you choose one action without waiting for motivation?
Think of a day when you don't expect anything to feel enjoyable. What could you tell yourself about doing something without requiring enjoyment?
Think of a moment when you feel numb. What thought could help you choose an action even if you don't feel much from it yet?
Think of a moment when you feel hopeless. What could you tell yourself that doesn't require you to suddenly feel hopeful?
Think of a moment when your brain says nothing will change. What could you tell yourself about what you actually know about the future?
Think of a moment when your brain says nothing matters. What could you tell yourself about doing one small thing that matters to you anyway?
Think of a moment when the future feels too big to think about. What could you tell yourself about getting through today?

Think of a moment when even the next hour feels difficult. What could you tell yourself about getting through the next ten minutes?
Think of a moment when you don't trust yourself to make a big decision. What could you tell yourself about postponing decisions until the intensity changes?
Think of a moment when you feel pressure to solve your entire life. What could you tell yourself about what actually needs to happen today?
Think of a moment when you can't see a solution. What could you tell yourself that leaves room for a solution you can't see yet?

Think of a situation where you believe silence will be awkward. What experiment could test whether a brief silence is actually a problem?
Think of a situation where you believe you need to keep a conversation going. What could you test by letting the other person contribute more?
Think of a situation where you believe you need to be entertaining, funny, interesting, or impressive. What could you do differently to test that rule?
Think of a situation where you believe people won't approach you unless you do all the work. What could you change and observe?
Think of something you're afraid to ask someone. What could asking teach you that guessing cannot?
Think of something you assume someone will say no to. What could you learn by respectfully asking?
Think of something you believe will annoy someone if you ask for help. What experiment could test that prediction?
Think of a situation where you believe asking a question will make you look stupid. What question could you ask and observe the response?
Think of a situation where you believe speaking up will cause conflict. What small opinion or preference could you express?
Think of a situation where you usually agree to avoid disagreement. What could you test by respectfully expressing a different view?
Think of something you want to say no to. What could you learn by setting one small boundary?
Think of a situation where you believe someone will be angry if you say no. How could you test that prediction safely?
Think of a situation where you believe another person's disappointment would be unbearable. What small limit could you set and observe what happens?
Think of something you believe you must explain or justify extensively. What could you test by giving a shorter explanation?
Think of a situation where you apologize even when you haven't done anything wrong. What could you test by not automatically apologizing?
Think of a situation where you believe you have to fix someone else's feelings. What could you do differently and observe?
Think of a situation where you believe someone's bad mood is your responsibility. What experiment could test what happens if you don't immediately try to fix it?
Think of a situation where you believe you need reassurance before you can move forward. What could you try before asking for reassurance?
Think of something you repeatedly ask others to confirm. What could you learn by waiting before asking?
Think of a situation where reassurance makes you feel better temporarily. What experiment could test whether the anxiety changes on its own?
Think of something you repeatedly check. What do you predict would happen if you checked once instead?
Think of something you check until it feels “right.” What could you learn by stopping before you feel completely certain?
Think of something you redo because you're afraid it isn't good enough. What could you submit, send, or finish without redoing it?
Think of something you reread repeatedly before sending. What could you learn by reading it once and sending it?
Think of a decision you keep reconsidering. What could you test by making a reasonable choice and not reopening it immediately?
Think of something you research repeatedly because you want certainty. What could you learn by stopping after a reasonable amount of information?
Think of a situation where you believe you need a backup plan for every possibility. What could you test by leaving one minor uncertainty unplanned?
Think of something you do “just in case.” What do you predict would happen if you didn't do it once?
Think of a safety behavior you use when you're anxious. What might happen if you reduced it slightly?
Think of something you carry, check, rehearse, avoid, or arrange to feel safer. What belief does that behavior prevent you from testing?
Think of a situation where you believe you can cope only if another person is with you. What small part could you try with less support?
Think of something you usually ask another person to do for you. What piece could you experiment with doing yourself?
Think of a place or activity where you rely heavily on a trusted person. What small increase in independence could you test?
Think of something you believe you can't start without motivation. What would happen if you worked on it for five minutes anyway?
Think of something you believe you can't do when you're tired, discouraged, or unmotivated. What tiny version could you test?
Think of a task you expect to be awful. What could you learn by doing it for ten minutes and rating the experience afterward?
Think of something you predict will take forever. How could you test the prediction by timing yourself?
Think of something you believe requires a huge amount of energy. How could you measure the energy it actually takes?
Think of something you've been procrastinating on. What do you predict you'll feel before, during, and after starting?
Think of something you believe you need to finish all at once. What could you test by doing only one piece?
Think of something you believe isn't worth doing unless you can do a lot. What could you learn from doing a very small amount?
Think of something you believe won't improve your mood. What activity could you try and rate your mood before and afterward?
Think of an activity you've stopped doing because you don't expect to enjoy it. What could you test by trying it briefly?
Think of something you used to enjoy but currently expect to feel nothing from. What could you notice besides whether you feel “happy”?
Think of an activity you expect to be pointless. What could you measure afterward besides enjoyment?
Think of something you believe you have to feel better before doing. What could you test by doing it while still feeling low?
Think of something you believe anxiety must decrease before you can function. What task could you try while allowing anxiety to remain?
Think of something you believe you can't concentrate on while anxious. What short task could test that belief?
Think of something you believe you can't tolerate while upset. What safe, manageable amount could you practice tolerating?
Think of an uncomfortable feeling you immediately try to change. What could you learn by observing it for a short time without fixing it?
Think of a body sensation that worries you. What safe activity could help you learn more about how the sensation changes naturally?
Think of something you believe will make your anxiety keep rising forever. What could you safely stay with long enough to observe what anxiety actually does?
Think of something you usually escape when anxiety becomes intense. What could you learn by staying a little longer?
Think of a situation where you believe anxiety means you can't continue. What small action could you take while anxiety is present?
Think of something you believe you must feel confident about before trying. What could you test while still feeling uncertain?
Think of something you believe you need certainty about before making a decision. What small decision could you make with incomplete information?
Think of something where you believe uncertainty itself is dangerous. What harmless uncertainty could you intentionally leave unresolved?
Think of a question you keep trying to answer in your head. What could you learn by allowing “I don't know” to remain for a while?
Think of something you believe you need to know right now. What could you test by waiting?
Think of something you fear you'll forget unless you keep thinking about it. What could you test by writing it down and redirecting your attention?
Think of a worry you believe helps you stay prepared. What could you test by preparing once and then reducing the worrying?
Think of something you believe worrying prevents. How could you compare what happens on a day when you spend less time worrying?
Think of a situation where you believe self criticism helps you perform better. What could you test by using a more neutral or encouraging inner voice?
Think of something you believe you'll stop trying at if you're kinder to yourself. What could you test?
Think of a task where you usually motivate yourself through pressure. What could you try instead and compare the result?
Think of a mistake you usually punish yourself for. What could you test by responding with problem solving instead?
Think of something you believe you need to feel guilty about in order to behave responsibly. What would responsible action without self punishment look like?
Think of a belief that says, “If I'm not hard on myself, I'll become lazy.” What experiment could test whether that's true?
Think of something positive about yourself that you have trouble believing. What behavior could help you gather evidence about that belief?
Think of a strength you aren't sure you have. What situation could give you a chance to test it?
Think of something you believe you're bad at. What would be a fair experiment rather than a test designed to prove yourself wrong?
Think of something you believe other people can do but you can't. What small attempt could give you new information?
Think of something you've labeled yourself as “not the kind of person who does.” What would happen if you tried acting differently once?
Think of a belief about yourself that may be based on old experiences. What current experiment could test whether it still fits?
Think of a belief about relationships that you've carried for a long time. What small, safe interaction could give you newer evidence?
Think of a belief that people can't be trusted. What low risk situation could help you gather more specific evidence rather than testing trust all at once?
Think of a belief that people will leave if you disappoint them. What small disagreement or boundary could provide useful information?
Think of a belief that people won't care if you reach out. What small action could test it?
Think of a belief that you're always the one who has to initiate connection. What could you change briefly and observe?
Think of a belief that nobody notices when you're struggling. What could happen if you gave one trusted person a clearer signal?
Think of a belief that asking directly for what you need won't work. What could you ask for clearly and observe?
Think of a belief that you have to hide your feelings to keep a relationship okay. What small, appropriate feeling could you communicate?
Think of a belief that conflict always damages relationships. What small disagreement could help you test whether respectful conflict can be tolerated?
Think of a belief that apologizing makes you weak. What could you observe after offering a genuine apology?
Think of a belief that admitting you don't know something will make people think less of you. What could you test?
Think of a belief that changing your mind will make you look foolish. What could you test by openly updating your opinion?
Think of a belief that you have to solve problems alone. What could happen if you involved someone else in one manageable problem?
Think of a belief that taking a break means giving up. What could you test by taking a planned break and returning afterward?
Think of a belief that slowing down will make you less productive. What could you compare after deliberately pacing yourself?
Think of a belief that you need pressure to get anything done. What could you test using structure instead of last minute pressure?
Think of a belief that rest has to be earned. What could you observe if you took reasonable rest before reaching exhaustion?
Think of a belief that saying no makes you selfish. What could you observe after saying no respectfully to one small request?
Think of a belief that putting your needs first will hurt someone. What small act of self advocacy could you test?
Think of a belief that other people always know better than you. What small decision could you make based on your own judgment?
Think of a belief that you can't trust yourself to make decisions. What low stakes choice could you make without seeking someone else's approval?
Think of a belief that you must know the “right” answer before acting. What could you test by choosing a reasonable option and adjusting later if needed?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What exactly do you expect to happen?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. How strongly do you believe it from 0 to 100%?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What would count as evidence supporting it?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What would count as evidence that doesn't fit it?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What experiment would give you useful information without being unnecessarily difficult?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What would make the experiment too easy to teach you anything?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What would make the experiment unnecessarily difficult?
Choose a prediction you'd like to test. What is a manageable middle ground?
Choose a behavioral experiment. What will you do differently from what you normally do?
Choose a behavioral experiment. What behavior will you not use so you can actually test the belief?
Choose a behavioral experiment. What should you pay attention to while you're doing it?
Choose a behavioral experiment. What could you record immediately afterward so your memory doesn't rewrite the experience later?
Choose a behavioral experiment. What happened compared with what you predicted?
Choose a behavioral experiment you've already tried. What surprised you?
Choose a behavioral experiment you've already tried. What evidence did you gather?
Choose a behavioral experiment that didn't go the way you hoped. What did you still learn?
Choose an experiment where your prediction came true. What did you learn about your ability to cope?
Choose an experiment where your prediction was partly true. What was different from what you expected?
Choose an experiment where your prediction was wrong. How could you help your brain remember that evidence next time?
What is one belief you would rather test than keep arguing with in your head?

promptDecks.title: Self-as-Context
promptDecks.description: Explore the difference between who you are and the thoughts, feelings, roles, labels, and experiences you have, building a more flexible sense of self that can hold change without being defined by it.

prompts.text: What words do you usually use to describe yourself?
What labels do you put on yourself?
Which labels feel helpful?
Which labels sometimes feel limiting?
What is the difference between saying “I am anxious” and “I am noticing anxiety”?
What is the difference between saying “I am a failure” and “I am having the thought that I failed”?
What is the difference between being an angry person and experiencing anger?
What is the difference between being insecure and noticing insecurity?
What happens when a temporary feeling starts to feel like your identity?
What thoughts about yourself are easiest to believe?
What negative descriptions of yourself tend to stick?
Where did some of those descriptions come from?
Which beliefs about yourself have changed over time?
What did you believe about yourself five years ago that you no longer believe?
What does it tell you that your beliefs about yourself can change?
What emotions have changed throughout your life?
What interests have changed throughout your life?
What relationships have changed throughout your life?
What parts of your life have changed dramatically?
What has been present through all of those changes?
Are you the same thing as any one thought you have about yourself?
Are you the same thing as any one emotion you experience?
Are you the same thing as your biggest mistake?
Are you the same thing as your greatest accomplishment?
Are you the same thing as what other people think about you?
Are you the same thing as your anxiety?
Are you the same thing as your sadness?
Are you the same thing as your anger?
Are you the same thing as something painful that happened to you?
Can something be an important part of your story without being your entire identity?
What is something you have experienced that does not define everything about you?
What is something you struggle with that is only one part of you?
What is something you are good at that is only one part of you?
What roles do you have in your life?
Who are you when you are not thinking about those roles?
What happens to your identity when one of your roles changes?
Who are you outside of school or work?
Who are you outside of your relationships?
Who are you outside of your accomplishments?
Who are you outside of your struggles?
Who are you outside of other people's expectations?
What remains when you temporarily set aside all the labels you use for yourself?
What is it like to notice that you are having a thought?
What part of you is able to notice what your mind is saying?
What is it like to notice yourself feeling an emotion?
What part of you can observe an emotion changing?
What happens when you watch your thoughts instead of getting pulled into them?
What happens when you notice “I am judging myself”?
What happens when you notice “My mind is comparing me again”?
What happens when you notice “Anxiety is here” instead of “I am anxious”?
What happens when you notice “Sadness is here” instead of “I am sad”?
Can you notice a thought without becoming the thought?
Can you notice an emotion without becoming the emotion?
Can you notice an urge without becoming the urge?
Can you notice a memory without being back inside the memory?
Can you notice a judgment about yourself without deciding it describes you?
What do you notice when you observe your experience from a little distance?
What changes when you become curious about yourself instead of evaluating yourself?
Can you notice two different feelings at the same time?
Can you have conflicting thoughts without either one defining you?
Can one part of you feel afraid while another part wants to move forward?
Can one part of you feel angry while another part still cares about someone?
Can you dislike something you did while still seeing yourself as more than that action?
Can you be struggling and strong at the same time?
Can you be uncertain about yourself without needing to decide exactly who you are?
What does it feel like to allow yourself to be complicated?
What happens when you stop trying to fit yourself into one description?
What would change if you did not have to prove what kind of person you are?
What would change if a difficult thought about yourself were allowed to come and go?
What would change if you treated your identity as larger than any one story your mind tells?
What would you notice about yourself if you stopped keeping score of your successes and failures?
What would you notice if you did not compare today's version of yourself with anyone else?
How would you respond differently to a mistake if you knew it could not define you?
How would you respond differently to criticism if another person's opinion did not determine who you are?
How would you respond to anxiety if anxiety were something you experience rather than something you are?
How would you respond to a painful memory if you could notice that the memory is happening in the present rather than the event happening again?
What becomes possible when you do not have to defend a particular version of yourself?
What parts of yourself are you still discovering?
What parts of yourself have surprised you?
What contradictions exist within you?
What is something true about you that does not fit the story you sometimes tell about yourself?
What evidence is there that you are more complicated than your harshest self judgment?
What is something you have done that does not fit a negative label you sometimes give yourself?
What is something you have learned that changed the way you understand yourself?
What is a version of yourself you once thought would last forever?
What might your current self descriptions look like ten years from now?
If your thoughts were a movie, what would it be like to watch from the audience instead of being inside every scene?
If your thoughts were words on a screen, who is noticing the screen?
If your emotions were weather, what part of you could be the sky that holds all of it?
If your experiences were chapters in a book, what is the difference between one chapter and the whole book?
If your life were a house, what experiences could visit without becoming the entire house?
If your mind were telling a story about who you are, what would it be like to notice yourself listening to the story?
If a painful label were written on a name tag, what would happen if you took the name tag off?
If all your roles disappeared for one day, what would still be there?
If your younger self and future self were both sitting beside you, what would all three versions of you share?
If you could watch your life from a little distance, what patterns would you notice without judging them?
If you were the container rather than the contents, what thoughts and feelings would you notice yourself holding today?
What is one label you would like to hold more lightly?
What is one thought about yourself you do not have to turn into an identity?
What is one emotion you can notice without letting it define you?
What is one mistake you can allow to be part of your story rather than the definition of your story?
What is one struggle you can describe as something you experience rather than something you are?
What is one part of yourself you would like to approach with more curiosity?
What is one reminder that you are bigger than what you are feeling right now?
What is one sentence you want to remember when your mind tries to tell you who you are?

promptDecks.title: Dreams
promptDecks.description: Explore hopes, possibilities, future aspirations, and the experiences you would love to pursue or create.

prompts.text: What is a dream you’ve had for a long time?
What dream feels most exciting to you right now?
If nothing could stop you, what would you want to do?
What is something you hope you get to experience at least once in your life?
What is something you would love to create, build, or bring into the world?
What is something you would love to become really good at?
Where is somewhere you hope life takes you someday?
What would your ideal life actually look like on an ordinary day?
What kind of person do you hope you become as you get older?
What kind of relationships do you hope to have in your future?
What do you hope there is more of in your future than there is in your life right now?
What do you hope there is less of in your future than there is in your life right now?
What is something about your life now that you hope never changes?
What would make you look back someday and feel proud of the life you lived?
What matters to you more than being successful?
How would you want your life to feel, not just look?
What is a dream that is more about happiness than accomplishment?
What is something you want for your future because you genuinely want it, not because other people expect it?
What is a future you could be happy with even if it looks different from what you once imagined?
What is something you hope your future self has figured out?
What do you hope your future self still cares deeply about?
What is something you hope your future self thanks you for doing now?
What is something you hope your future self has stopped worrying about?
